hypothesis: Five-session planning saves initial entry fees with SOXL/cash but ignores later conversion to the benchmark; a benchmark-terminal conversion value may eliminate this state bias without changing forecasts.

valuation.formula: After current fees, x=(SOXL,SOXX,cash). Expected terminal benchmark-converted dollar value = x1*(1+mu1)+(x2+(1-c)*x0*(1+mu0))/(1+c).
valuation.normalized_coefficients: q=1/(1+c); mu_eff=((1-c)*(1+mu0)-1,(1+c)*(1+mu1)-1). Cov_eff=diag(1-c,1+c)*Vmean*diag(1-c,1+c). Same solver objective scaled back by q equals expected conversion value minus relative-mean ambiguity penalty.
valuation.actual_fee_policy: Only real current rebalance fees enter realized NAV; hypothetical horizon conversion costs are never deducted as realized fees.
financial_inputs_unchanged: forecast uncertainty before exact valuation transform
not_claimed: not a hard terminal holding constraint

numerical_floor_scope: Only positive-effect classification changes; all raw returns, point estimates and CI values retained. Cumulative aggregate, each annual, leave-one-year and rolling log excess must exceed1e-8; bootstrap usesN*daily_lower>1e-8. PureSOXX floating noise never qualifies as alpha.
gate_definition: All existing complete2016-2022 SOXX net return/year/rolling/MaxDD/CVaR/bootstrap gates at bothcosts retained; numericalfloor only tightens zero comparison. Raw oldsign and qualified counts both reported. No production from reusedhistory.
label_precision: Same unchanged parent float64 daily/H5 labels and causal25features from qualifiednativeopens.
stopping: Exactly1new terminal-valuation candidate vs1same-forecast control at two costs, no refits or alternate terminal assumptions after outcomes. Preserve all failures and continue separate diagnosis toward user goal.
limitations: Terminal conversion is a planning valuation, not an executed future order or a promisedterminalportfolio.
Mean uncertainty still excludes future regime shifts and model selection uncertainty.
